mr brain: [date] clinical history: 55-year-old female with left parietal glioblastoma multiforme. comparison: mr brain, [date], and priors. technique: multiplanar mr images of the brain were performed on a 3 tesla magnet with and without gadolinium contrast using the following pulse sequences: 3-plane localizer, axial and coronal t2 flair, sagittal fspgr, axial diffusion, axial perfusion, axial 3-d fspgr, axial spectroscopy, axial and coronal post gadolinium. findings: stable appearance of left parietal craniotomy with underlying left parietal lobe resection cavity which extends towards the left lateral ventricle. persistent pericavitary t2 flair hyperintensity is noted, unchanged from previous imaging. postcontrast imaging reveals minimal rim enhancement surrounding the resection cavity, with no significant change in enhancement pattern compared to prior. perfusion-weighted imaging shows increased relative cerebral blood volume in the hyperintense t2 area adjacent to the resection cavity. no new distant foci of t2 prolongation or enhancement are observed. the ventricles and sulci remain stable in size. the left lateral ventricle demonstrates mild retraction towards the resection cavity. stable periventricular t2 prolongation is noted, with some nodular characteristics, unchanged from prior studies. no areas of reduced diffusion suggestive of acute infarct. impression: 1. since [date], stable minimal enhancement surrounding the resection cavity with no significant changes noted. 2. consistent findings with residual disease, characterized by pericavitary t2 hyperintensity and elevated relative cerebral blood volume. 3. spectroscopy results to be processed and reported separately.
